correctness.rationale: The regular language 1(1|00)* gives ordered V_m=V_{m-2} concatenated with 2^(m-1)+V_{m-1}. Its unique join gap is G_m. Each internal bridge at bit-length L occurs F_(L-m) times, and crossings of successive digit lengths contribute only gaps one or two, proving the complete finite histogram including K=1,2. Fibonacci ratios yield the limiting masses, unit total probability and the exact geometric tail. Independent predicate and token-construction verifier agrees for every K=1..15, with convergence at K=19. Finite tests corroborate but are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: OEIS A060142 fixes the exact underlying support and a Fibonacci-word positional connection, but its inspected definition, commentary, and program contain no adjacent-support-gap histogram or probability law. The present theorem is not a restatement of that support list: it computes a full family of finite histograms and an infinite-mean limiting return law. OEIS A086747 specifies the equivalent binary indicator. Targeted published literature and mathematical-record searches found no covering gap-distribution statement. A previously unindexed enumeration could still cover the claim.
residual_risks: OEIS A060142 exactly describes the base set; an unindexed appendix, difference transform or published enumeration of its gaps may exist even though no covering formula was found.
The original Baum–Sweet 1976 article and the entire Allouche–Shallit monograph were not inspected at full-text level; any relevant gap proposition there would supersede originality.
Independent literature review and independent proof verification have not been performed.

value.rationale: Return spacings of sparse automatic sequences are natural recurrence statistics: the Baum–Sweet word has unbounded zero runs and zero symbol-one density, so existence of gap types alone does not quantify typical gaps among support points. This theorem gives every finite dyadic-prefix gap multiplicity, resolves the duplicated smallest bridge at gap three, and identifies an explicit normalized infinite-mean heavy-tail law of exponent log_2(phi). These are complete, parameter-uniform recurrence statistics rather than a fixed numerical slice. Future studies of rare-event return dynamics and correlations can use the exact one-gap marginal. The original support-language/Fibonacci facts are not claimed as new.
